reference: Hodgkin, A. L., & Huxley, A. F. (1952). A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve. *The Journal of Physiology* 117(4), 500-544.
result_or_relation: The single-compartment membrane equation with Na⁺, K⁺ and leak conductances and the rate functions of the gating variables m, h and n. jaxfne uses the modern form: resting potential −65 mV, depolarization positive, E_Na 50 mV, E_K −77 mV, E_L −54.387 mV, integrated by forward Euler with the gates updated before the voltage

reference: Izhikevich, E. M. (2003). Simple model of spiking neurons. *IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks* 14(6), 1569-1572.
result_or_relation: Eqs. 1-3: $\dot v = 0.04v^2 + 5v + 140 - u + I$, $\dot u = a(bv - u)$, reset $v \leftarrow c$, $u \leftarrow u + d$ at $v \ge 30$ mV; the RS, FS and LTS parameters of Fig. 2 (`jaxfne.presets.CELL_TYPE_PRESETS`). The kernels take one forward-Euler step of `dt` for both variables and test for a spike after the update; the paper's network code takes two 0.5 ms steps for $v$ per 1 ms step of $u$

reference: Brette, R., & Gerstner, W. (2005). Adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire model as an effective description of neuronal activity. *Journal of Neurophysiology* 94(5), 3637-3642.
result_or_relation: The adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire cell: $C\dot V = g_L(E_L - V) + g_L\Delta_T e^{(V - V_T)/\Delta_T} - w + I$, $\tau_w \dot w = a(V - E_L) - w$, $w \leftarrow w + b$ at a spike. The refractory period and the clip of the exponential's argument follow Tahvili et al. (2026)

reference: Tahvili, F., Vinck, M., & di Volo, M. (2026). A mean-field model of neural networks with PV and SOM interneurons reveals connectivity-based mechanisms of gamma oscillations. *PLOS Computational Biology* 22(6), e1014378.
result_or_relation: Methods Eqs. 15-18 and Tables 1-2: the E, PV and SOM AdEx network with conductance synapses, synaptic delays and an external Poisson conductance drive. The kernel matches an independent transcription of this project's port of Eqs. 15-18 bit for bit (`tests/test_emitters_adex.py`); `decay="exp"` also offers the exact exponential decay of the conductances

reference: Wang, X.-J., & Buzsáki, G. (1996). Gamma oscillation by synaptic inhibition in a hippocampal interneuronal network model. *The Journal of Neuroscience* 16(20), 6402-6413.
result_or_relation: The coherence measure κ on binary spike trains in bins of width τ: the mean over cell pairs of shared active bins over sqrt(n_i n_j). jaxfne departs from the paper's use in three declared ways: the default bin width is 5 ms, cells with no spike in any bin are excluded from the mean, and the measure is NaN with fewer than 2 spiking cells

reference: Billeh, Y. N., et al. (2020). Systematic integration of structural and functional data into multi-scale models of mouse primary visual cortex. *Neuron* 106(3), 388-403.e18.
result_or_relation: The recurrent connection probabilities of the 17 V1 populations (E per layer; Pvalb, Sst and Htr3a interneurons per layer) and their lateral distance rule $p(r) = \min(1, A\,e^{-r^2/\sigma^2})$, with $A$ set so that the mean over 75 µm equals the literature value; transcribed from the release's build file. The orientation-tuning factor of E-to-E pairs is not applied

reference: Frank, E. (1952). Electric potential produced by two point current sources in a homogeneous conducting sphere. *Journal of Applied Physics* 23(11), 1225-1228.
result_or_relation: The potential on the surface of a homogeneous conducting sphere from a current dipole inside it, in closed form: the sum of the Neumann series $\sum_n (2n+1)/n\,(b/R)^n P_n(\cos\gamma)$ differentiated along the dipole. jaxfne models one shell only (no skull or scalp layers) and offers an average reference

reference: Hagen, E., Dahmen, D., Stavrinou, M. L., Lindén, H., Tetzlaff, T., van Albada, S. J., Grün, S., Diesmann, M., & Einevoll, G. T. (2016). Hybrid scheme for modeling local field potentials from point-neuron networks. *Cerebral Cortex* 26(12), 4461-4496.
result_or_relation: The hybrid scheme: the LFP of a point-neuron network as presynaptic spike counts convolved with per-connection laminar kernels of passive multicompartment cells, with line-source currents in an infinite homogeneous medium. jaxfne's cells are vertical cables with current-based exponential synapses, solved exactly on the time grid; the morphologies of the model (hybridLFPy `morphologies/stretched`) are reduced to depth profiles of membrane area and Rall-equivalent diameter

reference: Nicholson, C., & Freeman, J. A. (1975). Theory of current source-density analysis and determination of conductivity tensor for anuran cerebellum. *Journal of Neurophysiology* 38(2), 356-368.
result_or_relation: Current source density $-\sigma\,\partial^2\phi/\partial z^2$ in one dimension, by the three-point second difference along the contact axis. jaxfne omits $\sigma$ and pads the edges, so the output is a CSD proxy in the units of the potential proxy

reference: Sarvas, J. (1987). Basic mathematical and electromagnetic concepts of the biomagnetic inverse problem. *Physics in Medicine and Biology* 32(1), 11-22.
result_or_relation: The magnetic field outside a spherically symmetric conductor from a current dipole, volume currents included, in closed form. The field is independent of the conductivity profile and zero for a radial dipole. jaxfne returns the field component along each sensor's orientation

reference: Lindén, H., et al. (2014). LFPy: a tool for biophysical simulation of extracellular potentials generated by detailed model neurons. *Frontiers in Neuroinformatics* 7, 41.
